4. After some years the petitioners came to learn that the case property had been listed in the gazette of abandoned property buildings dated 23-11-86 in serial No. 246 of the 'Kha' list prepared and published by the Ministry of Housing and Public Works under Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 (Annexure-F). The petitioner's predecessor immediately filed an application before the Court of Settlement on 19-7-88 along with another application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing the application on the ground that he had no knowledge of the enlistment of the case property in the 'Kha' list (Annexure-G-G-1). The said application was registered as Complaint case No.1159 of 1982 in the Second Court of Settlement, Dhaka. During the pendency of the aforesaid Settlement case the predecessor of the petitioners died on 15-4-89 leaving behind the petitioners as legal heirs. 

 5. The learned Court of Settlement by its Judgment and order dated 27-2-94 rejected the application for being hopelessly barred by limitation as it was filed long after 108 days, the limitation period, provided in section 7(i) of the Ordinance No.LIV of 1985 (Annexure-H), from the date of publication of the gazette on 23-9-86. 

 19. Apart from the common jurisdictional error of the aforementioned type an administrative authority may step out of jurisdiction in various other ways, such as by acting in bad faith, dishonestly or for improper motive or by acting unreasonably, arbitrarily or capriciously. In the instant case, facts are that the predecessor of the petitioner was alloted and allowed to acquire and possess the property by due process of law. An enquiry was made by the respondents to find out whether the case property was abandoned or not and it was declared not to be an abandoned property by the respondents on the basis of the said report (Annexure-B). Later enlistment of the case property by the respondents in the 'Kha' list shows bad faith, dishonesty and improper motive on their part. The petitioners, therefore, do have a type of entitlement that should now be protected under due process of law. The right to enforce a fundamental right is another fundamental right which gives the petitioner right to move this court even though his application was rejected by Settlement Court on the ground of limitation.
